description: The INITIALIZE [category] TO VALUE phrase - a 2002 introduction. THE EDGE IS QUOTED from the edition texts (kb/Work PB3965): COBOL-85's INITIALIZE is INITIALIZE {identifier-1}... with at most a REPLACING phrase (§1985:VI.6.17.2), 'The INITIALIZE statement provides the ability to set selected types of data fields to predetermined values' (§1985:VI.6.17.1), and its only phrase is REPLACING, 'The key word following the word REPLACING corresponds to a category of data' (§1985:VI.6.17.4 GR1); the 2002 general format adds [{ALL | category-name} TO VALUE] (§2002:14.8.19.1), 'If ALL is specified in the VALUE phrase it is as if all of the categories listed in category-name were specified.' (§2002:14.8.19.3 GR2), and §2002:F.2 states the change, its item 73: 'INITIALIZE statement, VALUE phrase. A VALUE phrase may be specified in the INITIALIZE statement'. 2014 and 2023 keep it (§2014:14.9.19.3 GR2, §2023:14.9.20.4 GR2). Folded from the inline InitializeBinder gate (Exec Step E).

IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.
PROGRAM-ID. RWIVAL.
DATA DIVISION.
WORKING-STORAGE SECTION.
01 A PIC X(3) VALUE "ABC".
PROCEDURE DIVISION.
MAIN.
    INITIALIZE A ALL TO VALUE.
    STOP RUN.
